fixed.how:
Root cause: RepoProposals.consider deduplicated only its own offer key (repo-create.ts:323-327 at b0ecd2e). withdrawRepoOffers and withdrawLinked withdrew only the offer key, never an open repo.create change card of the command executor. All changes are in packages/runtime/src/loop/repo-create.ts:
- New asksForRepository(card, projectId): recognises an executor change card (email_token plus decision) whose command, or a part of a composed plan, is repo.create for the project. consider() now returns 'already_asked' while such a card is open, so the person's own card stays the one card.
- withdrawRepoOffers (via repoCardProject) now withdraws the project's open single repo.create change cards as well as the offer, once the project has a repository. The Inbox then shows 'Closed: it no longer needs you.'
- RepoProposals.withdrawLinked also drops the executor's closure behind a withdrawn or expired repo.create card (dropClosedClosures). It uses the new optional RepoCommandRunner.pending and cancel, which CommandLoop already has. Chat therefore no longer reads such a card back as waiting, and a late Yes or confirm is refused.
- RepoCreator.whenLinked(listener), registered by the RepoProposals constructor, does this at once when the creator links a repository. sync() does it at its next pass for a link made another way.
- compose.ts is untouched: compose already passes the RepoCreator and the CommandLoop.
Docs: ADR 0097 amendment, runtime.md (the repository offer), user guide.

fixed.problem: Review blocking 2 (R-rebuildcard). The rebuild card's new Redo did not do what its line says ('The task is done again from main; a session starts for it.'). Redo only reopened the task. The run then found the open PR on the task's branch, resumed from origin/<branch> and rebuilt it again. On the conflict variant (a dependent that edits its dependency's own file, the common chain) it stopped at the same conflict with a second card ('merge conflict in ...', I resolved it / Drop the branch and retry from scratch / Cancel the task). On the clean variant, the redo stacked a new commit on the rebuilt one instead of starting from main.

fixed.how:
Root cause: session/pr-answers.ts applyRedo reopened the task and nothing told the PR executor to start over. githost/pr-executor.ts resumes whenever an open PR is on the branch, unless the task's last rebase-conflict answer is 'dropped'.
Fix:
- applyRedo now marks the answered card with `redo_from_base: true`, in the same transaction. The new export is REDO_FROM_BASE_FIELD from @forerunner/capabilities.
- PrTaskExecutor.conflictAnswer reads the newest such card of the task as a 'dropped' answer. The next run starts the branch from origin/<base> (with any unmerged dependencies' work), and the open PR gets the new work by a forced push.
- The mark is consumed once a run reaches review or files a new conflict card, exactly as for 'Drop the branch and retry from scratch'.
- This applies to both rebuild cards, so the unchanged line is true for both. No words changed.
Docs: ADR 0111 amendment, runtime.md (the rebuild card), capabilities.md (the conflict answer), user guide.

not_done.problem: Edge, existing behaviour: if the Redo's run pauses (budget or a question) before it reaches review, the next run reads the unconsumed redo mark again and starts from main again, dropping the paused work in progress.
not_done.why: Same as the existing 'Drop the branch and retry from scratch' answer: 'dropped' stays in force until a run reaches review. Consuming the mark at branch creation would make the next run merge the old conflicting branch into the work in progress, which is worse. Left as it is and documented.

not_done.problem: Edge: if the person answers Yes on two repository cards for one project (for example Chat's and a previewed one) before any sync applies either, the second Yes still posts 'was not applied'.
not_done.why: Only open cards are withdrawn: an answered one belongs to the answered-cards sync. This is rare, needs two Yes clicks on two cards, and is not what the review found.
